text:
maria.support: FYI customer AcmeMaps hitting a lot of 429s and latency spikes since ~09:00 UTC. They say it started after a sync job. sample request_id: r-0a9c3, customer_id: acme-342. Can infra take a look?

josh.sre: looking now. Is it consistent across routes or focused on one (generate / embeddings / embeddings-batch)?

maria.support: customer says it's during `POST /v1/generate` and a few retries on embeddings. They provided curl + small payload repro.

kevin.eng: saw an alert from alert-bot at 09:07 for `High429Rate` on prod region-us. Could be quota exhaustion or burst enforcement.

alert-bot: ALERT: High429Rate prod-us (triggered at 2026-03-16T09:07:12Z) — rule: requests.status.429 rate > 50/minute over 5m (route=generate).

josh.sre: first quick checks: 1) prometheus query for 429 by customer/route:
```
sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{status=\"429\"}[5m])) by (route, customer_id)
```
2) tenant burst tokens: `redwood_tenant_bucket_tokens{customer_id=\"acme-342\"}`
3) check per-route latency: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`

devin.prod: can you paste the curl the customer ran? want to repro quickly.

maria.support: paste from ticket: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxxx' -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"sync full dataset"}' -H 'X-Customer-ID: acme-342'``` They ran ~40 concurrent workers for ~6 minutes during the sync.

josh.sre: 40 concurrent workers for 6m is a classic burst. If tenant has a token-bucket configured for burst=20 and refill 10/s, you'll see bursts of 429 until bucket refills.

kevin.eng: I pulled logs for r-0a9c3: `route=generate tenant=acme-342 status=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded token_bucket_empty`. Also saw L7 proxies returning 429 before hitting runtime.

josh.sre: that suggests enforcement at edge (rate limiter) rather than runtime OOM. For attribution, check `redwood_rate_limiter_ejected_requests_total{customer_id=\"acme-342\"}` and `redwood_rate_limiter_policy{route}`.

maria.support: customer is asking for root cause and whether we can increase their quota temporarily. Billing question?

carol.billing: from billing side, quota is tied to their subscription tier + reserved capacity. We can do a short-term uplift if account manager approves. Need exact time window and expected sustained RPS.

josh.sre: suggested triage steps: 1) run the prometheus queries above to confirm 429 distribution by route and tenant. 2) check Grafana dashboard panel "Limits — 429 by tenant/route" (dash link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/limits/429s) and open the timeseries for acme-342. 3) examine rate limiter configuration: `/etc/redwood/ratelimit/policies.cfg` or config API `GET /internal/ratelimits?customer=acme-342` 4) collect sample request traces (enable sampling) and X-Request-IDs for audit.

kevin.eng: ran query: `sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{customer_id=\"acme-342\",status=\"429\"}[5m])) by (route)` — spikes align with 09:00-09:06 window and are almost entirely `generate`. embeddings show a tiny bump.

maria.support: customer says they retried with exponential backoff but still saw many 429s. They attached their client logs showing retries at 200ms intervals.

josh.sre: exponential backoff at 200ms may be too aggressive for a global token bucket. Recommend they back off to 1s then jitter. Also recommend enabling client-side concurrency cap.

devin.prod: is there any sign of auth/billing misconfiguration? e.g., wrong API key mapping to a different tenant or quota baseline?

kevin.eng: checked auth logs: their API key maps correctly to acme-342 and quota plan=pro-annual. No auth failures. Billing shows usage within monthly credits but burst exceeded per-second limit.

josh.sre: to attribute throttle to route/model/customer run:
```
sum(rate(redwood_rate_limiter_tokens_consumed_total[1m])) by (customer_id, route, model)
```
then correlate with `redwood_requests_total{status!~\"2..\"}` to confirm failures.

maria.support: customers asks for mitigation now. Options?

josh.sre: short-term: 1) Request billing to temporarily raise per-second limit for acme-342 (fastest). 2) Apply a targeted route-level exception for their tenant for 10m via internal config API (require approvals). 3) Suggest they throttle client concurrency + backoff. Long-term: increase reserved capacity or adjust token-bucket params.

carol.billing: I can approve a 15-minute uplift to their per-second throughput if SRE confirms it will be safe for cluster. Need magnitude.

josh.sre: what's safe — current cluster headroom shows 25% spare on region-us if we accept a short-term 2x for that tenant. If you approve, I'll flip the policy to `burst=80, refill=40/s` for 15m against acme-342.

kevin.eng: before flipping, we'll run a quick canary: allow a single worker from acme-342 to run full concurrency for 60s to validate. If safe, we roll.

maria.support: told customer we're investigating and may be able to provide short uplift while we stabilize. They gave permission to temporarily increase.

josh.sre: action items: - kevin.eng to execute logs/queries and capture panel screenshots (DONE) - josh.sre to prepare ratelimit policy change and canary plan - carol.billing to issue 15m uplift - maria.support to update customer with ETA 20m

kevin.eng: panel screenshots: attached in ticket (png). Prometheus hits show 95% of 429s tagged route=generate and token_bucket_empty=true.

maria.support: customer accepted canary. starting canary now.

josh.sre: canary run results: 60s window had acceptable CPU/GPU load and no downstream queueing. Proceeding to flip policy for 15m.

alert-bot: INFO: RateLimitPolicyChange executed for customer acme-342 by josh.sre at 2026-03-16T09:28:14Z — new burst=80 refill=40/s (expires in 15m).

kevin.eng: post-change metrics show 429s dropped to near-zero for the customer during uplift; latency p95 improved from 420ms to 210ms.

maria.support: customer confirms error rate is down and sync completed. They're super grateful. :tada:

carol.billing: will follow up with account manager about a potential plan change; also logging a short invoice exception for the uplift window.

josh.sre: follow-up items: - add a Grafana alert runbook link into the alert message with quick mitigation steps. - consider auto-temporary-uplift workflow for high-trust customers (requires product). - recommend docs update: client best-practices for bursty syncs (concurrency + backoff patterns).

maria.support: closing loop with customer and moving ticket to resolved. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
